system_description.narrative_title: AI buildout vs. limits: finance, power, politics, market repricing
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant story is that the rapid AI infrastructure and financing boom is colliding with real-world limits — energy supply, credit market strain, regulatory backlash and electoral politics — producing a market repricing and IPO uncertainty. As an open system, flows of capital, compute demand, electricity, regulation and public sentiment feed back into corporate investment, debt issuance and valuations; shocks (midterm results, bond-market stress, supply shortages) propagate through these links. Systemic variables (capital flows, grid capacity, regulatory constraint, investor risk appetite) interact with concrete entities (data centres, chipmakers, banks, AI startups) and dated events (midterms, Anthropic IPO) to amplify or dampen the buildout.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: AI infrastructure buildout (data centres, servers), semiconductor supply, cloud providers and AI firms, investors and lenders, debt and equity markets, energy providers/grids, regulators and local voters, major IPOs and corporate earnings.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economy and capital markets (macroeconomic conditions, geopolitics, energy/climate systems and cross‑border finance).
adjacent_subsystems: Financial and credit markets (bonds, loans, private equity)

variables.name: Capital flow rate
variables.description: Net rate at which financial capital is moving into AI‑related investments and infrastructure projects.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: Average willingness of market participants to accept downside risk in AI‑exposed assets and strategies.

variables.name: Debt market liquidity
variables.description: Available depth and immediacy of credit supply for borrowers in markets financing AI activities.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: Average premium borrowers pay over risk‑free rates to access credit, reflecting cost of debt financing.

variables.name: Equity issuance rate
variables.description: Pace at which new equity (IPOs, follow‑ons) is being offered to finance AI companies and projects.

variables.name: Corporate AI investment rate
variables.description: Speed of corporate capital expenditure directed toward AI infrastructure, tooling and R&D.

variables.name: Data‑center construction rate
variables.description: Rate of ground‑up starts and completions of data‑center capacity relevant to AI workloads.

variables.name: Compute capacity utilization
variables.description: Share of installed AI compute capacity that is occupied by active workloads at a given time.

variables.name: Semiconductor supply stress
variables.description: Degree of constraint, delays and shortages in semiconductor production and distribution for AI hardware.

variables.name: Electricity grid load
variables.description: Aggregate electricity demand placed on local and regional grids by AI infrastructure relative to capacity.

variables.name: Energy generation margin
variables.description: Spare generation capacity available in power systems after meeting baseline demand, available for incremental AI load.

variables.name: Energy price level
variables.description: Prevailing prices for electricity and other energy inputs that affect the operating cost of AI infrastructure.

variables.name: Regulatory constraint intensity
variables.description: Severity and pervasiveness of regulatory restrictions, permitting requirements and legal limits on AI buildout and operations.

variables.name: Political backlash intensity
variables.description: Strength of public and electoral opposition to AI projects and perceived social impacts of AI expansion.

variables.name: Market volatility / fear gauge
variables.description: Level of market volatility and fear reflecting uncertainty about AI prospects and systemic financial risk.

variables.name: Valuation expectation gap
variables.description: Divergence between market prices of AI‑exposed assets and underlying fundamentals or discounted cash‑flow expectations.

catalysts.title: Anthropic IPO timing / valuation shock
catalysts.description: Anthropic's planned IPO and investor skepticism could either draw huge capital or be delayed/cut, shifting AI funding and market expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Anthropic reveals $900bn...', 'Exclusive: Anthropic IPO timing uncertain', 'AI backlash could threaten Anthropic IPO timing'.

catalysts.title: Political push to curb data‑centre buildout
catalysts.description: Elected Democrats and ballot defeats are prompting calls and actions to halt or limit new data‑centre projects, slowing AI physical expansion.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democratic governors elected on promises to stop data centre building', 'Top Democrats call to rein in AI buildout', 'Voters rebuff AI data centers'.

catalysts.title: AI credit repricing / wider credit spreads
catalysts.description: Signs of strain in the AI credit market and rising CDS activity point to a cycle of debt repricing that will widen spreads and tighten credit conditions for AI projects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'A chill wind in the AI credit market', 'AI-related debt binge may pressure European bond markets', 'AI is making CDS great again'.

catalysts.title: Market correction driven by AI fears
catalysts.description: A sharp rout in AI‑heavy tech indices and elevated fear gauges could continue, reducing liquidity, risk appetite and AI valuation multiples.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Investors wipe $2.5 trillion off Nasdaq', 'Nasdaq set to confirm correction', 'Tech-stock rout accelerates retreat from the AI trade'.

catalysts.title: Continued data‑centre construction delays
catalysts.description: Permitting, political opposition and project oversight are causing ongoing delays to data‑centre starts and completions, tightening near‑term capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'What the increasingly awkward data centre construction delays mean', 'Microsoft tightens oversight of neocloud data center projects', 'Voters rejected AI data centers'.

catalysts.title: Regulatory tightening on AI and content use
catalysts.description: Courts and governments are signalling stricter legal and policy limits on AI (copyright, sovereignty, school curbs), raising compliance costs and constraints.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'EU court advisor warns AI chatbot may breach copyright', 'Control and sovereignty to shape UK approach', 'Google curbs AI in school accounts'.

catalysts.title: Rising memory/chip costs and supply stress
catalysts.description: Unprecedented memory chip costs and semiconductor supply issues will pressure margins and increase hardware costs for AI buildout.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Apple warns ‘unprecedented’ memory chip costs', 'AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1 billion quarterly charge', 'Micron and other chip stocks slip'.

catalysts.title: Large corporate bond issuance to fund AI
catalysts.description: Major tech firms issuing multibillion‑dollar bonds to finance AI spending will reshape debt markets and funding flows in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Meta seeks to raise $9.2 Billion', 'Meta raises $15 billion', 'Oracle Looks to Raise $20 Billion', 'Apple raises $7.5 billion from bond sale'.
